title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
This sheet is out of place. The neighbouring pages are a typed English text on the Brauer group of a ringed space, apparently a thesis or preprint filed in the same folder. This page is a handwritten Grothendieck note on the group-theoretic structure attached to Hodge or motivic cocharacters. The opening line ('M^+ ⊂ P_lis …, correspondant à certaines classes de conjugaison d'hom.') seems to say that some class of (effective or positive?) motives or Hodge structures corresponds to certain conjugacy classes of homomorphisms G_m → G.

Setting: G is a reductive group over Q, presumably the Mumford–Tate (Hodge) group or a motivic Galois group. γ is the Hodge cocharacter G_m,C → G_C, and Σ is presumably a representation or a weight condition, with the hypothesis 'Σ ≥ 0' a positivity or effectivity condition.

The construction:
- Choose a maximal torus T of G. Put Γ = X_*(T_C) = Hom(G_m,C, T_C), the cocharacter lattice.
- W = (N(T)/T)(C) is the Weyl group.
- W' = (Aut(G,T)/T)(C), the automorphisms of G preserving T, modulo the inner ones coming from T.
- Then W ⊂ W', W'/W = Out(G)(C), and W' acts on Γ.
- One obtains a cone Γ^+ ⊂ Γ which contains γ, lies inside the region cut out by 'Σ ≥ 0', and is W-stable. Grothendieck warns that it is perhaps not W'-stable.
- Being W-stable, the cone corresponds to a 'saturated' subset of Γ' = Γ/W.
- Γ/W = [Hom(G_m,T)/(N_G(T)/T)](C) = [Hom(G_m,G)/G](C), the set of G(C)-conjugacy classes of cocharacters.
- This set is the C-points (= Q̄-points) of a non-connected, étale-type Q-scheme S. Hence π_1(Q, C) = Gal(Q̄/Q) acts on it, through a finite quotient (a splitting field of G).

The concluding claim is that the cone is stable under this Galois action. This is exactly the setting in which the reflex field is defined (the field of definition of the conjugacy class of μ). It is also the setting for the twisted '*-action' of Galois on X_*(T)/W through Out(G). The likely aim is to constrain which (G, conjugacy class of γ) can arise for motives, e.g. effective ones, via a Galois-stable positivity cone.
errors: The transcription line 'opère sur Γ = S(C) = S(Q̄)' should be read as Γ' = Γ/W = S(C). Γ itself is not the point set of S; the conjugacy-class set is.

Galois-stability of the cone is asserted, not proved. Galois acts on Γ/W through the *-action, which factors through Out(G) = W'/W. Grothendieck himself notes the cone may fail to be W'-stable, so Galois-stability needs an argument, e.g. that the condition Σ ≥ 0 is defined over Q (Σ a Q-rational representation) and that γ's Galois conjugates satisfy it. The page gives no such argument.
Hom(G_m,G)/G as a 'scheme' is informal: it is an étale sheaf or disjoint union of points over Q̄ (ind-finite étale over Q), not a finite-type scheme. This is harmless for the C-points statement.
Γ' is called 'non connexe sur Q'. It is in fact a disjoint union of countably many components, each finite étale over Q.

ideas.what: The set of G(C)-conjugacy classes of cocharacters equals X_*(T)/W; it is the Q̄-points of a Q-scheme with a Galois action factoring through a finite quotient.
ideas.modern_name: Galois (*-)action on conjugacy classes of cocharacters; field of definition of the conjugacy class of μ (reflex field)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Shimura (reflex field, 1960s); Deligne, 'Travaux de Shimura' (1971) for the group-theoretic formulation; Kottwitz (1984)
ideas.where_published: SGA 3 contains the scheme-theoretic tools (Aut(G,T), outer automorphisms, Weyl group schemes). The cocharacter-class formulation is not, to my knowledge, in his published texts.

ideas.what: W ⊂ W' = Aut(G,T)/T with W'/W = Out(G).
ideas.modern_name: Splitting of Aut(G) via pinnings; outer automorphism group

ideas.what: A W-stable cone of cocharacters containing the Hodge cocharacter γ and cut out by a positivity condition Σ ≥ 0, descending to a 'saturated' Galois-stable subset of conjugacy classes; meant to describe the cocharacter classes attached to 'positive' (effective?) motives.
ideas.modern_name: Constraints on Hodge cocharacters of Mumford–Tate / motivic Galois groups (cf. Serre's conditions on Hodge cocharacters)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (1971–79), Serre ('Propriétés conjecturales des groupes de Galois motiviques', 1994), Milne

missed.claim: Grothendieck sketches a positivity cone Γ^+ in the cocharacter lattice: it contains the Hodge cocharacter, is defined by a condition 'Σ ≥ 0', and is W-stable and Galois-stable. It apparently serves to characterize which conjugacy classes of homomorphisms G_m → G correspond to a class M^+ of (positive/effective) motives. This is an early group-theoretic attempt to describe the image of motives (or effective motives) in terms of motivic-group data.
missed.quote: on obtient un cône Γ^+ de Γ, invariant par W (mais peut-être pas par W'!) contenant γ, contenu dans l'hypothèse Σ ≥ 0 … Ceci posé, le cône envisagé est stable par π_1.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is an early (≤1971) instance of the reflex-field / Galois *-action on X_*(T)/W formalism applied to motives. That formalism is usually attributed to Deligne (1971) and, for motivic Galois groups, to Serre (1994). The idea of a Galois-stable effectivity cone among cocharacter classes does not appear as such in the standard literature on effective motives, so it is mainly of historical interest.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a fragmentary but genuine Grothendieck note. It handles conjugacy classes of cocharacters as Q-points of a scheme with Galois action, which is essentially reflex-field technology, in a motivic and Hodge context, possibly before or contemporaneous with Deligne's 'Travaux de Shimura'. The mathematics itself is now standard, and the page is too fragmentary to show a definite unpublished result.
transcription_corrections: The 'Γ = S(C) = S(Q̄)' after the deleted '[-S-]' should most likely read Γ' = S(C) = S(Q̄) (the quotient Γ/W).
Opening 'M^+ ⊂ P_lis' is uncertain. It may refer to a class of motives or of smooth ('lisse') objects; the reading is unclear.
This page is a handwritten Grothendieck sheet unrelated to the neighbouring typed pages on the Brauer group of a ringed space.
